title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly changing evidence base on whether generative AI interventions improve mathematics learning. The authors argue that conventional reviews and meta-analyses become outdated too quickly in this field because generative AI tools and the research literature are evolving very fast. To respond to this, they introduce LLAMA LIMA, a living meta-analysis that is updated regularly and follows PRISMA-LSR guidance.

The study synthesizes experimental and quasi-experimental studies in which human learners used generative AI for mathematics learning and were compared with control groups that did not use generative AI. The review includes studies from journals, conference proceedings, edited book chapters, and some preprints undergoing peer review. For Version 2, the authors identified 21 eligible studies contributing 38 effect sizes and 4,071 total participants. They used a Bayesian multilevel meta-regression approach to account for multiple nested effects within studies and to support cumulative updating over time.

The population spans multiple educational levels and contexts, including primary, secondary, undergraduate, and adult learners, making the overall population mixed. The interventions covered a range of purposes for generative AI in mathematics education, such as acting as a mathematics expert, tutor/feedback system, instructor, collaborative facilitator, or teacher-support tool. Because this paper is a meta-analysis, it synthesizes studies conducted in varied settings and countries rather than a single implementation context.

The main conclusion is that generative AI-based interventions show a positive but still uncertain overall effect on mathematics learning (pooled g = 0.42, 95% credible interval [0.13, 0.72]). The authors found no strong evidence of publication bias, though a model-averaged estimate was somewhat smaller. They emphasize that the evidence base remains limited and heterogeneous, so robust general conclusions and moderator analyses are not yet possible. The paper’s broader contribution is methodological: it demonstrates a living meta-analysis model for keeping educational evidence syntheses current in a fast-moving AI domain.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems, including large language models and chatbots, used for mathematics learning in roles such as mathematics expert, adaptive assessment/tutoring, instructor, collaborative facilitator, or teacher support.
identified_tools.use_case: This living meta-analysis synthesizes experimental and quasi-experimental studies of generative AI-based interventions for learning mathematics across heterogeneous tools and implementations; it does not report per-tool results.

findings.finding_summary: Across 21 studies contributing 38 effect sizes, generative AI-based instructional interventions showed a positive pooled effect on mathematics learning outcomes of g = 0.42. The 95% credible interval was [0.13, 0.72], indicating substantial uncertainty, and the included studies covered 4,071 participants.

In publication-bias analysis using RoBMA, the model-averaged effect estimate was smaller but still nonnegative at g = 0.29, with a 95% CI [0.00, 0.68]. The inclusion Bayes factor for publication bias was BF = 0.65 with posterior probability = .39, which the authors interpret as weak evidence against publication bias.
findings.measure: Mathematics learning outcomes / mathematics performance (publication-bias-adjusted model-averaged estimate)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis following PRISMA-LSR guidelines with a Bayesian multilevel model and 21 included studies. Quality is slightly tempered because it is a living preprint and includes some preprints among the primary studies.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effect on mathematics learning outcomes was g = 0.42, which meets the threshold for medium impact. Although uncertainty is wide, the central estimate is clearly above 0.20.
